correctness.rationale: The full 2026 primary harmonic nonvanishing Lemmas 4.8 and 4.12 separate ambient harmonic degrees under great-circle Fourier restrictions: all even degrees >=2 and odd degrees >=5 are excluded while 0,1,3 survive. A trace-free symmetric cubic T restricted to n-perpendicular circle gives first Fourier center (3/4)Pi trace_P(T)=-(1/4)grad_S Y3; fourth-circle-moment identity establishes it. On S², integral Pi a=8pi*a/3 and div(-(1/4)grad Y3)=3Y3 because Laplacian eigenvalue -12; orthogonal L2 splitting yields exact norm and invertibility. For any a,Y3, choose R large enough to make Hess_S h+hI positive, proving range surjectivity. Independent exact direct fourth-moment for xyz with n=(0,3/5,4/5) yielded center (-3/25,0,0), matching formula. It does not replace the general analytic proof.

Their primary full fourteen-page text, including sections 4–5, does not present the 10-dimensional center-field range, its divergence inverse, norm isometry, or coherence-to-ball inference. Published cubic curvature/brightness findings address different observables. The center-field tomography is therefore a best-of-knowledge addition rather than a novelty claim for harmonic classification.

value.rationale: Recovers all observable nonradial geometry from continuously varying projection rotation centers, with an exact finite-dimensional inverse, radius ambiguity and orthogonal stability identity. It is a natural inverse-tomography invariant, not merely recomputing a known example.

The field determines the body up to the constant-radius support-function term and coherent centers characterize balls.
